name: Ironpass Reinforced Thermal Work Shirt
description:
A heavy-duty Henley-collar thermal designed for workers in cold-storage logistics, outer-corridor construction, and lake-exposure infrastructure work. The body is a dense waffle-knit synthetic-wool blend that traps body heat aggressively; the shoulders and elbows are reinforced with double-layered ripstop panels bonded at the seam. The three-button Henley placket allows ventilation when lifting. Color options are limited: charcoal, rust, and a muddy olive that workers call 'corridor green.' The cuffs have a thumb loop integrated into the hem.

Ironpass is a workwear-only label distributed through supply depots and union hall commissaries across the Tier 2 corridor. It does not advertise. Its reputation is entirely word of mouth and the fact that a well-maintained Ironpass thermal has been known to last seven years in active field use. It does not look glamorous. It feels like being held.
what_it_says: You work for a living and you dress accordingly. No apologies.
story_hooks: A body is recovered from a collapsed outer-corridor section; the Ironpass thermal survived intact when almost nothing else did, and the union wants to know why the section collapsed at all.
Ironpass has just lost its supply depot contract to a cheaper Stratum subsidiary — workers are quietly furious and some are talking about more than just switching brands.
A character finds an Ironpass thermal in a dead relative's belongings, washed and folded, with a union card sewn into the lining.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian heavy-weight thermal with pronounced waffle-knit texture across the torso, creating a deeply dimensional silhouette. The Henley collar sits slightly higher than a standard crew neck, framing the shoulders with deliberate industrial presence. Reinforced shoulder and elbow panels create subtle bulk in those zones—visible as squared-off panel edges at the seams. The overall impression is purposeful, worn, and built to absorb punishment.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with a slight taper at the waist; accommodates layering and movement without restriction. Sleeves are straight-cut with integrated thumb loops at the cuff hem, designed for gloved hands. The fit prioritizes function over form—comfortable for 12-hour shifts, not fashion.
physical_description.primary_material: Dense waffle-knit synthetic-wool blend (60% recycled polyester, 40% lab-grown wool substitute). Shoulders and elbows feature double-layered ripstop composite, bonded at critical stress seams.
physical_description.texture: Deeply textured waffle-knit creates air pockets visible to the eye; running a hand across it feels substantial and slightly rough. The ripstop panels are smoother, tighter weave. Slight pilling visible on well-worn examples at friction points (underarms, cuffs).
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal (deep gray-black), rust (oxidized orange-brown), or muddy olive-green ('corridor green'). No branding visible; colors are muted and practical—designed not to show dirt or grease stains.
physical_description.closures: Three-button Henley placket at the neckline in matte polymer or brushed metal; allows partial unbuttoning for ventilation during heavy exertion. No other closures.
distinctive_features: Double-layered ripstop reinforcement panels at shoulders and elbows, visibly bonded at seams
Thumb loops integrated into both cuffs—a single-purpose design detail for gloved workers
No visible branding or logos—reputation is entirely earned
Waffle-knit depth creates natural thermal insulation visible in the fabric structure
Seams are reinforced with visible topstitching in matching thread
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional—working-class essential. Not luxury, not salvage. Built for Tier 3 laborers in cold-exposure infrastructure roles.
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals affiliation with unionized cold-storage, construction, and waterfront work. Worn by people who work outdoors in the GLMZ winter. The seven-year lifespan is legendary in worker communities; wearing one signals reliability and experience. No pretense.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered when actually in use—cuffs may show fraying, minor pilling at stress points, small stains from oils or rust dust. The garment improves slightly with age as the waffle-knit softens. A pristine Ironpass thermal is either new or rarely worn.

A gloved hand rests on a metal railing, thumb hooked through the cuff loop. Background: frost-rimed shipping containers and gray sky. Mood: utilitarian, lived-in, reliable.
